title: Generation of human-induced pluripotent-stem-cell-derived cortical neurons for imaging
author: Wali, Li, et al.

steps.title: Coat plates with extracellular matrix
steps.instruction: Prepare poly‑L‑ornithine (15 µg/mL) and mouse laminin (10 µg/mL) coating solutions according to Tables 1 and 2 for the chosen plate format, then sequentially coat the wells.

substeps.instruction: Refer to Tables 1 and 2 for the volume of poly‑L‑ornithine and laminin to add per well (e.g., 100 µL per well for 96‑well plates).
Add 100 µL poly‑L‑ornithine solution to each well and incubate 2 h at room temperature (20 °–25 °C).
Aspirate the solution and wash wells twice with DPBS (‑/‑).
Optional: leave poly‑L‑ornithine coating in the hood overnight (16–18 h) at room temperature, sealing with parafilm.
Add 100 µL mouse laminin solution (10 µg/mL) to each well and incubate 2 h at room temperature (20 °–25 °C).
Do NOT wash laminin; aspirate the laminin solution immediately before adding the cell suspension to avoid drying the surface.
Note: thaw laminin stock at –20 °C overnight (16–18 h) at 4 °C before dilution in DPBS (+/+); do not dilute in DPBS (‑/‑). Alternative laminin‑521 (10 µg/mL) may be used.

steps.title: Immunostain mature cortical neurons
steps.instruction: Fix, permeabilize, block, and stain neurons in 96‑well plates using the Cytofix/Cytoperm kit and specified antibody dilutions.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate culture media and wash wells once with DPBS (‑/‑).
Add 100 µL Cytofix solution to each well; incubate 25 min at room temperature (20 °–25 °C).
Aspirate Cytofix and wash cells twice with DPBS (‑/‑).
Add Cytoperm solution (100 µL per well) to permeabilize and block; incubate 30 min at room temperature (20 °–25 °C).
Optional pause: plates can be stored at 4 °C overnight (16–18 h) before proceeding.
Prepare primary antibodies diluted 1:1000 in Cytoperm solution.
Aspirate Cytoperm and add 100 µL of the diluted primary antibodies to each well; incubate 1 h at room temperature (20 °–25 °C).
Wash wells twice with Cytoperm solution.
Prepare secondary antibodies diluted 1:500 in Cytoperm solution.
Add 100 µL diluted secondary antibodies to each well; incubate 30 min at room temperature (20 °–25 °C).
Wash wells twice with Cytoperm solution.
Prepare Hoechst diluted 1:10 000 in Cytoperm solution.
Add 100 µL Hoechst solution to each well; incubate 10 min at room temperature (20 °–25 °C).
Wash wells twice with Cytoperm solution.
Add 100 µL Cytoperm solution to each well for storage.
Seal plates with parafilm, protect from light with aluminum foil, and store at 4 °C. Image within 48 h to avoid fluorochrome fading.

steps.title: High‑throughput imaging of neurons
steps.instruction: Acquire fluorescence images of the stained 96‑well plate using the Perkin Elmer PhenixPlus system.

substeps.instruction: Place the plate on the PhenixPlus microscope equipped with a 16‑bit Andor Zyla 5.5 MP sCMOS camera and a 20× water‑immersion objective.
Set digital binning to 2× (resulting in 2160 × 2160 pixel images).
Capture z‑stacked images for each well to cover the full depth of the neuronal culture.
Acquire at least 15 fields of view per well.

steps.title: Analyze neurite morphology
steps.instruction: Use Harmony software (built into PhenixPlus) to segment nuclei and neurites and quantify neurite parameters.

substeps.instruction: Open the maximum‑projection images (generated from the z‑stacks) in Harmony.
Segment nuclei with the “Find nuclei” building block: test all four pre‑defined methods, select the one that visually best identifies nuclei, and verify across multiple fields and wells.
If needed, adjust nuclei area, threshold, and contrast parameters for optimal segmentation.
Segment neurites with the “Find neurites” building block using the settings shown in Figure 2C (or the default parameters if they work).
Measure neurite outgrowth parameters: total length, roots, segments, extremities, and branching.
Record the measurements for early neurons (Day 1 post‑seeding) and mature neurons (Day 15 post‑seeding).

steps.title: Assess neuronal maturation markers
steps.instruction: Quantify the proportion of neurons expressing mature cortical markers TBR1 or CTIP2.

substeps.instruction: Label neurons with Hoechst (nuclei) and either TBR1 or CTIP2 antibodies (as in Figure 3A–F).
Image the stained wells using the same microscope settings as for neurite imaging.
Segment nuclei using the “Find nuclei” building block (as described in step 4).
Apply the “Calculate Intensity Properties” building block to obtain fluorescence intensity of TBR1 or CTIP2 within each nucleus.
Set an intensity threshold based on an isotype control to define positive staining.
Calculate the percentage of marker‑positive cells: (number of TBR1/CTIP2‑positive nuclei ÷ total Hoechst‑positive nuclei) × 100.
Optional: repeat the pipeline for additional mature markers (BRN2, SATB2, CUX1).

description: The pluripotent stem cell-derived cortical neural progenitors used in the following protocol were generated according to the methods described by us1 and others.2Note: The cortical neural progenitors and mature neurons should be cultured in a humidified 37°C incubator with 5% CO2.Note: All procedures should be performed in a sterile environment. All waste materials should be considered potentially biohazardous and disposed according to the laboratory’s waste disposal policy.
